publish.youtubeTitle: I gave Claude Code a messy spreadsheet. 4 minutes later, a dashboard.
publish.youtubeDescription:
A real Claude Code session, start to finish. A cleaning company's 2026 job log (a sample: 214 jobs, three date formats, £ signs, Y/yes/NO/part in the paid column) goes in, and one prompt in plain English asks for a dashboard: money in by month, who still owes what, and the busiest cleaners.

Claude Code worked for 3 minutes 45 seconds, wrote 737 lines to one index.html, and the dashboard opens with a double-click. It found £2,955 still owed across 20 unpaid jobs, with the Patel family owing the most (£643).

The prompt and the setup are in Claude Codex Mastery: https://www.skool.com/yar-ai-automation-school-9911/about
publish.linkedin:
A cleaning company's job log became a live dashboard in 3 minutes 45 seconds.

The sheet was the usual mess: 214 jobs, dates in three formats, prices with and without £ signs, and a paid column that said Y, yes, NO or part.

I gave Claude Code one prompt in plain English:
→ money in by month
→ who still owes me, and how much
→ which cleaners are busiest
→ clean up the dates, prices and paid column as you go

It wrote 737 lines to a single index.html that opens with a double-click. £2,955 still owed across 20 unpaid jobs. The Patel family owes the most, £643.

The honest part: some jobs were only marked "part" paid, and the log never says how much. Claude didn't guess. It kept them out of the totals and told me to add an "amount paid" column.

That's the job worth selling. Not another AI app, one spreadsheet an owner hates.

Link is in the comments 👇

demo.prompt: This is my cleaning company's job log for 2026. Turn it into a one-page dashboard in index.html that I can open by double-clicking: money in by month, who still owes me and how much, and which cleaners are busiest. Clean up the messy dates, prices and the paid column as you go. Don't run any commands.
